title: Royal Flying Doctor Service: Guardians of the Sky
author: Aaron
body:
Of all the iconic outback institutions Australia is blessed with, the Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) is surely one of the first that comes to mind. Connecting our rural residents to vital healthcare services, the RFDS has been saving lives for more than 90 years. Utilising its own fleet of aircraft, the RFDS ensures distance need not be a reason for people missing out on the benefits of the latest medical technology.

Operating in some of Australia’s most remote areas, APT’s Kimberley & Outback Wilderness Adventures (KOWA) has a close working relationship with the RFDS. On occasion, KOWA has been the beneficiary of their essential services, such as when needing to address the health concerns of its guests. It’s comforting to know they can quickly respond if needed and that the impressive scope of their operations takes in even the most far-off regions of our country.

All of KOWA’s Driver Guides engage in fundraising for the RFDS while on tour. A stand-out in that area has been Gary Annett, who has managed to raise an incredible $66,000 for the RFDS since 2016 through photographic calendar sales alone.

With a third of its operating budget being dependent on fundraising, philanthropy and corporate partnerships, the RFDS relies largely on the generosity of the community to continue delivering its high quality of service, which sees it continue to help 1,000 people each day.

While it is largely known for its fleet of aircraft, the RFDS also utilises 140 healthcare road vehicles and delivers a wide range of services including GP and nurse clinics, dental, Telehealth, and mental health and wellbeing services.

One of the little known, yet critical aspects of its work involves the stocking of 3,500 medical chests, strategically distributed among tourist venues, general stores, post offices, and other venues throughout Australia. These mini-pharmacies contain such life-preserving items as snakebite kits, antibiotics, painkillers, and defibrillators.

The APT Foundation is proud of its association with the Royal Flying Doctor Service, recognising the great value it brings to the wider community, as well as the importance of supporting its crucial work.
